messages.subject: Question about physignal function
messages.body_plain:
HI everybody

I was trying to run this line of the physignal function:

plot(PS.shape$PaCA, phylo = TRUE)

But I got one error plus several warnings

Error in plot.window(...) : need finite 'xlim' values

In addition: Warning messages:

1: In min(x) : no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf

2: In max(x) : no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf

3: In min(x) : no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf

4: In max(x) : no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf

5: In plot.window(...) : "phylo" is not a graphical parameter

I used this line with the corresponding xlim and ylim values

plot(PS.shape$PaCA, phylo = TRUE, xlim=c(-0.1,0.1), ylim=c(-0.1,0.1))

but I got these warnings:

Warning messages:

1: In plot.window(...) : "phylo" is not a graphical parameter

2: In plot.xy(xy, type, ...) : "phylo" is not a graphical parameter

3: In axis(side = side, at = at, labels = labels, ...) :

  "phylo" is not a graphical parameter

4: In axis(side = side, at = at, labels = labels, ...) :

  "phylo" is not a graphical parameter

5: In box(...) : "phylo" is not a graphical parameter

6: In title(...) : "phylo" is not a graphical parameter

I tried to use the geomorph dataset (plethspecies) with plot(PS.shape$PaCA, phylo = TRUE)

but I got exactly the same error, can somebody tell me where the error is? Is this related to my geomorph version (3.1.2)? BTW, I successfully obtained summary(PS.shape)and plot(PS.shape)

Thanks!!

Paolo

messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Question about physignal function
messages.body_plain:
Pablo,

I was able to get the same error as you but it worked fine if the code was changed to:

plot(PS.shape$PACA, phylo = TRUE)

A key difference is that I am using version 3.3.1, installed from Github.  We did indeed have a $PaCA object in the previous version (3.3.0) that we have since changed as a result of Phylogenetically-aligned Component Analysis being changed to Phylogenetically Aligned Component Analysis, using the acronym, PACA, as a result of the review process for our recently accepted paper.  I suspect that the problem is you are using a help file that does not correspond to the version of geomorph you are using because neither $PaCA nor $PACA were part of the physignal output in version 3.1.2.  You would get the same error trying to plot an object that does not exist, e.g., plot(PS.shape$this.is.sure.to.work <http://this.is.sure.to.work>, phylo = TRUE).

You might consider making sure you are using a help file with the same version (at the bottom of the help file) as the geomorph version you are running.

Cheers!
Mike

messages.subject: Change symbols in plotTangentSpace function
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I ran a PCA on ~80 species using the plotTangentSpace function. So far, so good. But, with so many different species, the plot is a bit unclear and I would like to try to add symbols for families. I tried to play with things like "pch= ..." but nothing is working. Any idea how to change the symbols?

spnames<-identmean[,1]
family<-identmean[,2]

col.gp <http://col.gp> <- rainbow(length(levels(spnames)))
names(col.gp <http://col.gp>) <- levels(spnames)
col.gp <http://col.gp> <- col.gp <http://col.gp>[match(spnames, names(col.gp <http://col.gp>))]

T1symm<-plotTangentSpace(Sym_Shape, axis1 = 1, axis2 = 2, warpgrids = F, mesh = NULL,label = spnames, groups = col.gp <http://col.gp>, verbose=T, legend=F)

The goal would be to add a "(length(levels(family)" amount of different symbols, and display a legend with the meaning of these symbols.

Thanks a lot!

Aurélien

messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Change symbols in plotTangentSpace function
messages.body_plain:
Hi Aurélien,

plotTangentSpace is depreciated, but you can use gm.prcomp and plot to get the morphospace you’re looking for. The argument pch will work in the plot function. Below is code showing you how you can define the shape of each tip according to family and add a legend. This assumes that there are 4 families (a, b, c, and d) and the shapes you desire are pchs 1:4. Obviously, edit as you see fit:

pch.gp <http://pch.gp> <- as.character(family)
pch.gp <http://pch.gp>[which(pch.gp <http://pch.gp> == levels(family)[1])] <- 1
pch.gp <http://pch.gp>[which(pch.gp <http://pch.gp> == levels(family)[2])] <- 2
pch.gp <http://pch.gp>[which(pch.gp <http://pch.gp> == levels(family)[3])] <- 3
pch.gp <http://pch.gp>[which(pch.gp <http://pch.gp> == levels(family)[4])] <- 4

PCA <- gm.prcomp(coords)
plot(PCA, main = "PCA", pch = pch.gp <http://pch.gp>)
legend(x = .02, y = .02, legend = c("a", "b", "c", "d"), pch = 1:4)

Best,
Erica

A slightly more generalized version of the code above would something like below. It assumes your Family information is in dat$Family (as a factor), and it you will have to correct the x and y for the new geomorph PCA output.

This should generate unique symbols and colors for all your families.

plot(x=gpa$PCscores[,1],
     y=gpa$PCscores[,2],
     col=dat$Family, cex=1.2,
     pch=as.integer(dat$Family))

legend('top', legend = levels(dat$Family),
       col = 1:length(levels(dat$Family)), cex = 1,
       pch = as.factor(levels(dat$Family)))

messages.subject: interlandmark distances
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I’m comparing several interlandmark distances between different groups of fish. I’m using the interlmkdist function and it works fine. However, I’m not sure whether I should use raw coordinates or the new corrected coordinates I get after performing Procrustes superimposition. I’ve tried both and I’ve noticed in few cases I got different results. Any suggestions?

Many thanks

Best wishes

Paolo
messages.body_snippet:

I’m comparing several interlandmark distances between different groups of fish. I’m using the interlmkdist function and it works fine. However, I’m not sure whether I should use raw coor

messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] interlandmark distances
messages.body_plain:
Paolo, what you use will depend on what your objective is with this comparison.

After superimposition scaling, position and rotation effects are accounted for, so that´s why you are seeing differences. If your objective is to compare these interlandmark distances as if they were actual biometric traits measured on the fish, you should use the raw coordinates.

Hope this helps

Antigoni

messages.subject: Problems with my data
messages.body_plain:
Hi all! My skills for R are pretty basic…not to say almost absent. Despite this, I need to start working with geomorph. After reading for a while I manage to create a list counting my data and the classifiers I need. The problem is that when I try to perform the GPA on my coordinates I get an error that reads "Error in colMeans(x) : 'x' must be numeric”. I know it must be a pretty silly m mistake, but I can not find what is wrong with my data.
I am using 3D Landmark coordinates exported from MorphoJ, so they should be ok, but I keep getting that error….

There are the scripts I am using:

X01Th <- as.matrix(read.table("01Txt Posdoc/01Thmj", header=T))
X01Th
names <- X01Th[,1]
X01Thcoords <- arrayspecs(X01Th[,3:ncol(X01Th)], 35, 3)
dimnames(X01Thcoords)[[3]] <- names

classifier <- read.table ("01Txt Posdoc/Id01Thporpoises.txt", header=T, row.names=1)
View(classifier)

X01Thlist <- list("landmarks"=X01Thcoords,"sp"= classifier[,1], "MF"=classifier[,2], "Fam"=classifier[,3], "habitat"=classifier[,4])

Y.gpa <- gpagen (X01Thlist$landmarks)
This is where I get, "Error in colMeans(x) : 'x' must be numeric”.

I would very much appreciate if any of you could give me advice on how to fix it.

Thank you in advance.

Dra. María Constanza (Kata) Marchesi

messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Problems with my data
messages.body_plain:
It appears there is an issue with the data you read in, such that R does not feel it is numeric.  When R reads in a text file, it attempts to turn numbers into numeric values, but if there is any value in a column of a spreadsheet that appears to be a character rather than a number, it will turn every value in that column into a character.

This could be a result of having missing values, if you have a character when landmark coordinates should be.

You can investigate with is.numeric for your landmarks.  Here is an example where I make an array that is numeric and then change it:

> x <- array(rnorm(20), c(5,2,2))
> is.numeric(x)
[1] TRUE
> x[1] <- "missing"
> is.numeric(x)
[1] FALSE

> x
, , 1

     [,1]                 [,2]
[1,] "missing"            "0.167187891186449"
[2,] "0.772530738306184"  "-2.14732054936248"
[3,] "0.51998572902904"   "-0.883942178639918"
[4,] "0.799570374946029"  "0.767075767637589"
[5,] "-0.440745963644269" "-0.781177725413061"

, , 2

     [,1]                 [,2]
[1,] "-0.201741650322557" "0.0533631979446144"
[2,] "1.18247522633732"   "-0.686812457661712"
[3,] "-1.26116603932832"  "0.22465234341027"
[4,] "0.419119275558514"  "0.651938264942584"
[5,] "-2.65182603096169"  "0.845655893573979"

Notice how if one value is not numeric, they are all not numeric (have quotes).  I’m afraid you have to scan your data in such cases and look for peculiarities.

Best,
Mike
